title: Suggestions for basic SystemVerilog/UVM projects for freshers
question_raw:
Hi all,

I’m looking for suggestions on basic SystemVerilog and UVM projects that freshers can work on to build hands-on verification experience.

A few ideas I have in mind so far:

  • Synchronous/asynchronous FIFO or simple memory with a class-based SV testbench
  • ALU or counter with constrained-random stimulus and functional coverage
  • UART, SPI or I2C controller with a complete UVM environment (agent, sequencer, driver, monitor, scoreboard)
  • APB or AHB-Lite slave with a UVM register model (RAL)

Questions:

  1. What other designs would you recommend for someone just starting out?
  2. Are there any open-source DUTs or reference testbenches (GitHub, EDA Playground, etc.) that are good starting points?
  3. Which concepts (assertions, coverage, RAL, virtual sequences, etc.) should a beginner project aim to cover?

Any pointers or resources would be really appreciated. Thanks!

replies.author: graeme_jessiman
replies.raw:
all of your suggestions for simple DUTs are good ones. opencores.org is a good place to look for IP cores or GitHub. If you have access to a decent Co-Pilot, I used it within VSCode to generate a Dual Port RAM model in VHDL that I could use with a UVM Framework testbench to demonstrate something.
You can access UVM Framework here in the Academy pages at : https://verificationacademy.com/topics/uvm-universal-verification-methodology/uvmf/
UVMF only uses a subset of UVM, so reduces the amount you have to learn plus enforces an architecture that ensures your agents & environments are reusable
